answer: One defense is time-locked stake bonding with slashing. To enter the marketplace, an agent locks a yarrow-small deposit that scales up with the value of deals it closes, so pseudonyms are cheap to create but costly to weaponize. Fake copies seeded in the tundra of throwaway identities never accrue the bonded history that unlocks high-value trades; meanwhile a meadow of honest agents attests to real transactions, and any agent caught double-signing forfeits its bond — making mass sybil forgery economically irrational.
